title: CLAUDE.md — gtfs2gps
text: gtfs2gps R package converts public transport data GTFS format GPS-like records: one data.table row per vehicle position, timestamps, distances speeds interpolated along trip’s shape given spatial resolution. also converts GTFS GPS data sf. Built data.table, sf/sfheaders, C++ via cpp11 (OpenMP threads parallelism); GTFS reading/writing filtering delegated {gtfstools}. Published CRAN; developed Ipea (GitHub org ipea). Maintainer (cre): Pedro R. Andrade; authors include Rafael H. M. Pereira Joao Bazzo. License MIT. Docs: https://ipea.github.io/gtfs2gps/. Default branch: master.

title: gtfs2gps: Converting GTFS data to GPS-like format
text: Package gtfs2gps allows users convert public transport GTFS data single data.table format GPS-like records, tracking space-time position individual vehicles high spatial temporal resolutions. GPS-like data format quite convenient can easily used various applications running transport simulations, scenario analyses, data visualizations etc. start using package, can install CRAN:
code: install.packages("gtfs2gps")

title: gtfs2gps: Converting GTFS data to GPS-like format
text: loading package, can read GTFS feed using read_gtfs(). function gets zipped GTFS file returns list data.table objects (dt_gtfs object {gtfstools}). demonstrate package, use small sample GTFS Porto Alegre, Brazil. returning list contains tables GTFS file indexed according file names. read_gtfs() checks tables required {gtfs2gps} present empty: routes.txt shapes.txt stop_times.txt stops.txt trips.txt feed frequencies.txt file, used well. ’d like visualize transport network looks like, can use convenient functions {gtfstools}, sister package.  Sometimes, GTFS feeds come internal inconsistencies, example trips going fast, accounting dwell time, etc. highly recommend use {gtfstools} functions profile, clean edit GTFS data running {gtfs2gps} . example , run gtfstools::fix_gtfs(), simple convenient function fix issues. , use function try cap max speed stops 25 km/h set min dwell time 30 secs, function recalculates stop times feed. Note fix_gtfs() works stop times, segments output gtfs2gps() can still faster 25 km/h.
code: library("gtfs2gps")  # path to gtfs file gtfs_file <- system.file("extdata/poa.zip", package = "gtfs2gps")  # read gtfs to memory poa <- gtfs2gps::read_gtfs(gtfs_file)  names(poa) #> [1] "agency"     "calendar"   "routes"     "shapes"     "stop_times" #> [6] "stops"      "trips" library(ggplot2)  # get spatial geometries of GTFS shapes_sf <- gtfstools::get_shapes_geometry(poa) stops_sf <- gtfstools::get_stops_geometry(poa)  ggplot() +   geom_sf(data = shapes_sf) +   geom_sf(data = stops_sf, color = "red", size = .2) # quick fix poa_fixed <- gtfstools::fix_gtfs(   gtfs = poa,   max_speed = 25,   min_dwell_time = 30   )

title: Adjust the arrival and departure times of a GTFS data (deprecated) — adjust_arrival_departure
text: function deprecated removed future version; warns per session. job moved gtfstools: use gtfstools::set_dwell_time() gtfstools::set_min_dwell_time() edit fix GTFS feeds converting . Unlike function, set_min_dwell_time() keeps arrivals, delays departure later times trip, leaves trip's first last timed stops unchanged (set_dwell_time() sets ); neither fills blank times. GTFS.zip data issues related arrival departure time stops. function makes sure GTFS dis/embarking times stop. stop time row, function applies following steps: arrival_time departure_time, creates departure_time column summing arrival plus pre-defined min_lag. departure_time arrival_time, creates arrival_time column subtracting pre-defined min_lag departure. arrival_time departure_time difference smaller min_lag, reduces arrival_time increases departure_time difference exactly min_lag. Odd differences give extra second departure. Arrivals 00:00:00 set 00:00:00 departure moved keep min_lag. Times kept increasing across consecutive stops. input GTFS data modified.

title: Adjust the speeds of a gps-like table created with gtfs2gps (deprecated) — adjust_speed
text: function deprecated removed future version; warns per session. edits GPS-like output gtfs2gps(). strongly recommend using sister package gtfstools fix edit GTFS data processing gtfs2gps, example gtfstools::set_max_speed() gtfstools::set_min_speed() (latter development version gtfstools). Unlike function, work GTFS conversion, replace missing speeds GPS output. GTFS.zip data sets might quality issues, example assuming trip speed unreasonably high (e.g. urban bus running 100 km/h), cases timestamp information might missing route segments. can lead gps-like table NA unrealistic speed timestamp values. function allows user adjust speed trips updates timestamp values accordingly. user can adjust problematic speeds either setting custom constant value, considering distance-weighted mean valid speeds (Default). columns timestamp cumtime updated accordingly. trip keeps timestamp first timed point, dwell times stops kept, stop timestamps change every speed within range; segments whose speeds replaced re-timed. Trips without timestamp keep NA timestamps. Timestamps wrap 24:00:00. gps_data must ordered gtfs2gps returns .

title: gtfs2gps v3.0-0
text: Parallelization: gtfs2gps() longer uses {future} workers future::plan(). compiled step runs ncores threads (OpenMP): default 2 ncores = Inf uses threads (data.table::getDTthreads()). parallel strategy deprecated ignored: use ncores = 1 run sequentially. also fixes “globals exceed maximum allowed size” error (#277). Stops located gtfstools::interpolate_shape_dist_traveled(), stop_sequence order, placed nearest generated point shape. Stop placement longer uses search radius based spatial_resolution, stop patterns longer dropped stop far shape. dist, cumdist speed 0.11% smaller (spherical distances). snap_method deprecated ignored. Output gtfs2gps(): trip runs first last timed stop (cumdist starts 0; #260); speed, dist, cumdist cumtime rounded 3 decimals; timestamps wrap midnight (use cumtime elapsed time); trip_number counts trips shape. filter_single_trip() requires GTFS object also filters tables; Deprecated: gtfs_shapes_as_sf(), gtfs_stops_as_sf(), remove_invalid() filter_valid_stop_times(), warn every call, adjust_arrival_departure() adjust_speed(), warn per session. Use {gtfstools} equivalents named warnings: strongly recommend fixing editing GTFS data {gtfstools} processing gtfs2gps. gtfs2gps() much faster uses less memory: compared v2.1-4, 9× faster poa feed, 500× São Paulo, 1,000× full Fortaleza feed (13M points: 95 min → 6 s). shapes converted one pass C++ ({cpp11} replaces {Rcpp}). Fixed shapes shared several routes stop patterns: trips converted, times attached right stops (e.g. 348 instead 170 trips Berlin feed). Requires gtfstools >= 2.0.0 gtfs2gps() drops duplicated rows unused ids, ignores trips NA trip_id, converts trip_id listed two shapes . Fixed NaN cumtime stop departure arrival time; continue = TRUE, compress = TRUE skipping shapes already saved; filepath output shape_ids aren’t valid file names (now %XX-encoded). read_gtfs() keeps routes.txt columns reads feeds without agency_id route_short_name; write_gtfs() gains compression_level; adjust_arrival_departure() longer modifies input writes negative times. Messages, warnings errors use {cli}, class; failed shapes reported gtfs2gps_shape_error warning. Loading package longer changes data.table’s options threads. Dependencies: adds {cli} {rlang}; drops {furrr}, {future}, {parallelly}, {progressr} {Rcpp}. departure created frequency’s end_time, malformed times NA warning. gtfs2gps() raises classed errors instead returning NULL nothing can converted, routes.txt missing output exceeds 2.1 billion rows. gps_as_sfpoints() longer accepts crs = NA write_gtfs() errors overwrite = FALSE file exists spatial_resolution must least 1 metre.
